title: Hear What the Lord in Vision Said
description: Hear What the Lord in Vision Said in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 89, part 5, headed “Christ's mediatorial kingdom; or, His divine and human nature”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hear what the Lord in vi-sion said, And made his mer-cy known: "Sin-ners, be-hold your help is laid "On my al-might-y Son.

lines: Hear what the Lord in vision said,
"High shall he reign on David's throne,
"My arm shall beat his rivals down,
"My truth shall guard him in his way,
"While, in my name thro' earth and sea
"Me for his Father and his God
"Call me his rock, his high abode;
"Firm as the heavens his throne shall last,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
